newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo sees more disposals at Amic.
newsitem.headline: Anglo sees more disposals at Amic.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday that its Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd (Amic) unit would see more disposals this year.
Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said in his annual statement that Amic, like the wider Anglo group, was carrying out a strategic review of its operations.
"Some disposals have taken place (at Amic) and more can be expected over the next year," he said.
Thompson said the group was seeking to become more flexible in the changing economic and political environment of South Africa and the world.
"Looking ahead, Anglo American is striving to ensure that net earnings growth will continue and that we will outstrip our major local and international competitors," he said.
Thompson added that Anglo's high exploration budget of more than $200 million a year was a sign of this commitment.
The group's gold mining operations have gone through a series of changes as the local gold mining industry indulges in a exchanges or sales in order to optimise profitability.
Thompson said there was a "sea-change" for the local industry, with the biggest move being Elandsrand's buy of Deelkraal.

In the group's platinum business, a planned merger of the firm's four listed companies in Anglo American Platinum Corp (Amplats) and its three administered producing firms stood to benefit the division.

"(It) will ensure greater operational flexibility, take Amplats further down the cost curve and place it in a better position to take advantage of a platinum supply deficit forecast to appear in the medium term," he said.
